newsitem.title: INDIA: India could ban coffee exports if needed - minister.
newsitem.headline: India could ban coffee exports if needed - minister.

text.p: The Indian government could impose a ban on coffee exports or allow imports if necessary to ensure domestic supply and stable prices, the commerce minister said on Monday.
"I can ban exports if necessary and also allow imports," B.B. Ramaiah told a planters' conference in this southern Indian town.

Earlier this month, the federal government freed the coffee trade from controls, allowing growers to directly market all their produce without surrendering part of it to a state agency as in the past.
This has raised fears that the freeing of the coffee trade would lead to unchecked exports and a domestic coffee shortage.
Ramaiah said he was hopeful that a mechanism would be worked out among the trade, growers and exporters to ensure enough domestic supplies and reasonable price stability.
